overall: Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing shellfish license applications in executive session under the preliminary screening purpose on April 23; minutes were also found inadequate and ordered amended and released.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee entered executive session for an improper purpose on April 23 when it reviewed shellfish license applications under the preliminary screening purpose.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that such discussions should not have occurred during the executive session and the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Office reviewed the April 23 executive session minutes in camera and found them too thin, though the complaint did not raise this point.
allegations.key_passage: they do not offer a sufficiently detailed summary of the Committee’s two-hour discussions, and instead simply state that the Committee reviewed the applications and then listed those applications in order of status.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Law’s requirements.
Publicly release the April 23 executive session minutes, without redaction or withholding.
Amend the April 23 executive session minutes to comply with G.L. c. 30A, § 22(a).
Certify to the AG within 60 days that the minutes were amended and released.
remedy_passage: The Committee is ordered to revise the executive session meeting minutes and to certify to this office within sixty (60) days of the date of this letter that it has amended and released the minutes.
